prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: WUI decision support; time sync, health checks, audit of assignment/staging changes; command continuity over automation when degraded; human confirmation always. Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): primary UI, triage; Airspace Restricted State (helitack sees boundary, confirms); produces Crew Staging Pin; promotes fire location for aviation review; records assignment packages; flags assignments on Confirmed Ignition State change. Disconnected mode: last sync shown, cached review, queued updates, no irreversible releases; conflicts held for Redtail. Access: RBAC, MFA, least privilege; offline expiring signed credentials; admin changes separately approved. Append-only audit store; field components forward signed records unmodified. North Lookout Camera Mast: Thermal Spot Snippet, smoke bearing. South Lookout Camera Mast: bearing track, Camera Cleaning Log to Smoke Classifier Module. Masts send health telemetry. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): Battery Swap Ticket, readiness; never authorizes crew movement. Drone Tasking Service: missions pending/active/complete; not flight-release authority; degraded: validates Drone Corridor Permit. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): advisory scores/perimeter; Ridge Shadow Mask; keeps last approved model; rejects unsigned packages. Smoke Classifier Module: never sole basis for aircraft commitment. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): Wind Shift Bulletin, exposure flags. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): fallback relay; queues acks ≥15 min. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): blocks incomplete releases; Runway Release Note (used by Tanker Base Manager in acceptance); Suppression Drop Receipt (used by County Emergency Liaison in post-incident reconciliation). East Retardant Loading Pump: Retardant Batch Slip to Tanker Base Manager; metered recirculation mode. West Retardant Loading Pump: shift-change inspection. Crewline Mobile Tablet: assignments, cached staging, encrypted queue. Actors: County Emergency Liaison, Duty Detection Officer (Orion), Air Attack Supervisor, Drone Pilot Operator, Tanker Base Manager, Helitack Crew Leader. Training seasonal/role-based; exercises. Governance board (ops, maintenance, infosec, detection/aviation/ground/county reps) approves seasonal rollout after risk/staffing/baseline/corrective-action review. Acceptance: Portal, Lantern, Classifier functional tests; masts, Brindle availability/timing/quality thresholds;

New part:
S239: Each after-action review shall reconstruct the timeline from system logs, user accounts, communications records, and maintenance notes without assigning blame to individual operators.
S240: Review facilitators shall document what was expected to happen, what actually happened, why differences occurred, and which corrective actions are necessary before the next readiness cycle.
S241: Corrective actions shall be entered into a controlled improvement backlog with assigned ownership, target completion dates, verification methods, and linkage to the originating event.
S242: Data stewardship shall define retention, access control, quality review, and disposition rules for operational records, sensor data, model outputs, configuration records, and user activity records.
S243: Operational data used for model evaluation shall be protected from unauthorized alteration and shall preserve enough context to support later engineering review and regulatory inquiry.
S244: Changes to the Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine or Smoke Classifier Module shall be evaluated with representative seasonal data before deployment to confirm that detection performance improves without unacceptable increases in false alerts.
S245: Configuration changes to field equipment shall be versioned, reviewed, and tested in a nonoperational environment before being promoted into the seasonal baseline.
S246: At the end of each fire season, the governance board shall compare system performance, operational workload, maintenance burden, and user feedback against the acceptance criteria approved for that season.
S247: The resulting improvement plan shall define which procedures, training materials, interfaces, algorithms, and support arrangements will be revised before the next seasonal readiness campaign begins.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
